title: Duel Decks: Mirrodin Pure vs. New Phyrexia: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: She is the apex of the artificer's craft, the spirit of the divine called out of base metal.
Reminders of Memnarch's reign still skirr across Mirrodin, reminiscent of his form if not his power.
"We sculpt the land into what we need—homes, armament, fortresses of war. Our strength comes not only from knowing, but from commanding the terrain." —Raksha Golden Cub, leonin kha
"We lost our homes and our kin. We won't let those rotters take our future as well."
"An appropriately detailed model is indistinguishable from reality, and much easier to control."
Mephidross gives up treasure easily... as long as you take its place.
The myr are like quicksilver: malleable in function and adaptable in form.
Scholars say that arbiters exist on every world, created by an unknown hand to enforce justice.
A great mirage, a dream of wings and silver.
The goblins say it used to be larger, before it began to stoke the Great Furnace with pieces of itself.
A mirror to draw its eye, a rod to rouse its rage, and a sword to break its bonds.
"Anything that watches without sleep and fights without fear is a valuable ally against the Phyrexians." —Kara Vrist, Neurok agent
The ultimate treasure is one that guards itself.
Venser wondered if it could still be called a teleportation spell if the destination is oblivion.
Some blades seek their own wielders.
"Phyrexians can't corrupt what they can't get close enough to touch."
For the first and last time, the horrific creature experienced terror.
Those who survive the test bear a mark of power anyone can recognize.
"Let their mindless armies come and face the might of genius." —Varil, Neurok partisan
Bladehold houses a rogues' gallery filled with the living "statues" of the worst enemies of the Auriok.
Lymph, the fluid essence of blinkmoths, is prized by wizards for the rush of intellect it provides.
Obsessed with the pursuit of knowledge above all else, vedalken can appear to be cold and emotionless.
After the Battle of Liet Field, the white sun crested above Taj-Nar, bringing hope to all who survived the carnage.
Taj-Nar, throne of Raksha Golden Cub, destined leader of the leonin prides.
A beacon in the night, a dream in the fog.
Lumengrid, site of the Knowledge Pool, source of vedalken arcana.
"The final stage of the illness: delirium, convulsions, and death." —Phyrexian progress notes
"Our archers made sport of it as it fumbled its way up the slag ridge. As it collapsed we thought ourselves safe, but the foul thing carried more than necrogen." —Adaran, Tangle hunter
For the Phyrexians, death is not an end, nor a one-time occurrence.
They watch for a new master, one more sinister than the last.
Phyrexia wastes nothing. Its food chain is a spiraling cycle.
Its precious corpses dance like puppets to attract mindless nim prey.
They once sought to unite with the flame of transcendence. Now they seek only to extinguish the lights of others.
Phyrexia's spiral of consumption grows ever wider and darker.
Where nature impedes, Phyrexians overcome.
"Meat *and* eggs. We eat!" —Borborygmos
Zombies mourn for the living and celebrate those who will soon be given the gift of death.
"Death—an outmoded concept. We sleep, and we change." —Sitrik, birth priest
"Your life was meaningless, but your death will glorify Yawgmoth." —Tsabo Tavoc
Even the dead are raw materials for the Phyrexian vision of perfection.
"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process." —Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
"In the game of conquest, who cares about the pawns if the king yet reigns?" —Geth, keeper of the Vault
Everything will find its use in Phyrexia. Eventually.
Life is ephemeral. Phyrexia is eternal.
"Under the suns, Mirrodin kneels and begs us for perfection." —Geth, Lord of the Vault
